acceptance: `RunTimeoutError` is importable from one documented public module, and the docs use it.
context:
Found while documenting --timeout (benchbox-site #233).

Owner decision 2026-11-22 (choice dialog): "benchbox.core.exceptions": move RunTimeoutError there next to the other exceptions; base class stays Exception (not BenchBoxError); run_deadline imports it; docs import from benchbox.core.exceptions. No top-level export. The STOP gate is satisfied.
description:
## Problem
`adapter.run_benchmark(timeout_seconds=...)` and `benchmark.generate_data(timeout_seconds=...)` raise `RunTimeoutError`, which is the documented Python outcome of a timed-out run, but it is defined in `benchbox/utils/run_deadline.py` and exported from neither `benchbox` nor `benchbox.utils`. The site docs (benchbox-site #233) import it from `benchbox.utils.run_deadline`, an internal module path.

## Change
Export it from the place BenchBox's other public exceptions are exported (find the existing convention first), update the docs that import it, and list it on the public contracts page.

## Decision gates
Follow the existing public-exception convention; if none exists or it is ambiguous, STOP and ask the owner which module is public. No re-export shims beyond the chosen public path.

## Verification rubric
A test imports `RunTimeoutError` from the public path and catches it from a timed-out `generate_data` stub; docs import from the public path; `make pr-preflight` exits 0.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
